name: bollinger_squeeze_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: After a Bollinger Band squeeze (bandwidth contracts to 20-bar low), the first breakout often fails and reverts. This happens because low-vol environments attract breakout traders who pile in, but insufficient momentum causes a mean reversion to the midline. In Indian large-caps, algos front-run the breakout causing an overshoot followed by reversion. Edge persists because breakout traders and mean reversion traders are structurally different populations with different timeframes.
mechanism: Bollinger band extremes indicate price has moved beyond 2 standard deviations from its recent mean. This typically results from a liquidity-driven overshoot rather than fundamental revaluation. Market makers and statistical arbitrageurs recognize the overshoot and trade against it, while the original directional flow exhausts, creating a natural mean-reversion within 30-90 seconds.
weaknesses: Squeeze can resolve into a genuine breakout instead of reverting — especially on news days
The 20-bar lookback on 1-min data is noisy; false squeeze signals in choppy markets
Limited trade frequency — squeeze setups may only appear 1-2 times per day across the universe
prior_art: Bollinger Band squeeze (John Bollinger); failed breakout mean reversion is well-documented
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
